title: One layout for all cards, resizable columns

message.text: Plan: the framework already has a columns system with resizable column boundaries and width words, so I would make every card page, top-level or sub, one column set built by the same recursive code. That set would be the card's detail plus its chat, with sub-cards opening as the next column. Each boundary would get the columns system's resize handle by default. The chat gets a sensible default share, about a third, so it is not a cramped strip beside a big empty space. No new layout code. A minion will first read the columns docs and the top-gap work now finishing, then build this in one pass. It goes ahead unless you say stop, and I'll show you before-and-after screenshots.

Landed, live and uncommitted. Every card and sub-card at any depth now uses the same Card.content(), with no separate sub-card layout. Both column seams have resize handles, and headless drags moved both. The chat defaults to a third of the card page (`clamp(22em, 33cqi, 64em)`, 909px at 3440) and the detail takes the rest. The write-up is `public/framework/ai2/doc/columns-seams.md`. The Live card's transcript now renders markdown too. The chat placement question (option A or B) is still yours.
